title: Greetings and politeness
context:
# Greetings and politeness

In Portugal the greeting follows the clock. **Bom dia** until lunch, **boa tarde** from lunch until dark, **boa noite** after dark — and «boa noite» is both *good evening* when you arrive and *good night* when you leave. **Olá** works at any hour.

With friends and family you use *tu*: **Tudo bem? / Como estás?** With strangers, older people, shop assistants and your boss you use *o senhor / a senhora* and the third person: **Como está?**

- **Bom dia, senhora Silva! Como está?** — Good morning, Mrs Silva! How are you?
- **Olá, Tiago! Tudo bem?** — Hi, Tiago! Everything OK?
- **Estou bem, obrigada. E tu?** — I'm fine, thank you. And you?
- **Um café, por favor. — Obrigado! — De nada.** — A coffee, please. Thank you! You're welcome.
- **Com licença, posso passar?** — Excuse me, may I pass?
- **Desculpe, não percebo. Pode repetir?** — Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat that?
- **Até logo!** (later today), **Até amanhã!** (tomorrow), **Adeus!** (for a long time)

**Watch out**

1. **Obrigado** if you are a man, **obrigada** if you are a woman. The word agrees with the person who is thanking, not with the person being thanked.
2. **Desculpe** apologises; **com licença** asks permission to pass or to come in. They are not interchangeable.

keyItems.note: after dark, both hello and goodbye
estar, because it is how you feel now
obrigado if the speaker is male, obrigada if female

keyItems.support: excuse me (may I pass / come in)

exercises.prompt: What does the word in bold mean?
exercises.explanation: «Olá» is a neutral hello: you can use it at any time of day, with friends and with strangers.

exercises.prompt: Match each greeting with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: «Bom dia» is used until lunch, «boa tarde» from lunch until dark, «boa noite» after dark.

exercises.prompt: It is nine in the morning. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: «Dia» is masculine, so it takes «bom»; «boa» goes with «tarde» and «noite».

exercises.prompt: It is 9 a.m. Greet Rita.
exercises.explanation: Before lunch you say «bom dia»; «dia» is masculine, so never «boa dia».

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Por favor» is 'please'. «De nada» answers a thank-you and «com licença» asks to pass.

exercises.prompt: Answer the thank-you. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: «De nada» (literally 'of nothing') is the standard reply to «obrigado» and «obrigada».

exercises.prompt: You are a woman. Thank the waiter warmly.
exercises.explanation: A woman says «obrigada», a man «obrigado»; «muito» never changes.

exercises.prompt: Put this short exchange between two friends in order.
exercises.explanation: The greeting comes first; «E tu?» sends the question straight back to the other person.

exercises.prompt: You are speaking to an older man you call «o senhor». Ask how he is (two words).
exercises.explanation: To a stranger or an older person you use the formal «Como está?»; «Como estás?» is the tu form, for friends.
exercises.givenAnswer: Estou bem, obrigado. E a senhora?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and correct it.
exercises.explanation: «Dia» is masculine, so the greeting is «bom dia». «Boa» belongs with «tarde» and «noite».

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: It is four in the afternoon, so «boa tarde»; «tarde» is feminine and takes «boa».
exercises.template: São quatro da tarde. ___ ___, senhor Costa!

exercises.prompt: What does the chunk in bold mean?
exercises.explanation: «Com licença» asks permission to pass or to come in; «desculpe» is for apologising.

exercises.prompt: Ask an older neighbour on the stairs to let you pass.
exercises.explanation: «Com licença» + «posso passar?» is the polite way to get past someone; «desculpa» is informal and is for apologies.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: How you feel right now uses «estar»: «Estou bem». Men say «obrigado», women «obrigada».
exercises.question: Como estás hoje?

exercises.prompt: Match each polite formula with its use.
exercises.explanation: «Desculpe» apologises, «com licença» asks permission. Both are polite, but they are not interchangeable.

exercises.prompt: You will not see this person again today. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: «Até logo» and «até já» are for later the same day; when you meet again only the next day you say «Até amanhã».
exercises.template: Hoje não te vejo mais. Até ___!

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and correct it.
exercises.explanation: «Obrigado» agrees with the person who is thanking, so a woman says «obrigada», whoever she is thanking.

exercises.prompt: You bump into a stranger. Apologise formally and say you did not mean to.
exercises.explanation: «Desculpe» is the formal apology; to a friend you say «Desculpa». «Foi sem querer» = 'I didn't mean to'.

exercises.prompt: You are at the door of an office. Ask politely if you may come in.
exercises.explanation: «Posso entrar?» asks permission to come in, and «por favor» makes it politer.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold (you are speaking to a stranger).
exercises.explanation: «Desculpe» apologises. «Com licença» only asks permission to pass or come in, so it cannot say sorry.

exercises.prompt: A visitor arrives at an office. Put the dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: The visitor greets and asks permission, the host answers «entre», and «obrigado» is always followed by «de nada».

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boa tarde! Com licença, posso entrar?

exercises.prompt: Tiago is a friend. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: With a friend you use «tu»: «Como estás?». «Como está?» would be for a stranger or someone older.

exercises.prompt: It is evening. Say goodbye to your teacher and tell her you will see her tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: After dark «boa noite» also works as a goodbye, and «até amanhã» says when you meet again.

exercises.prompt: Rita is speaking to her boss. One word is wrong.
exercises.explanation: With a boss you stay formal: «Como está?». «Como estás?» (tu) is only for family and friends.

exercises.prompt: Write your own greeting.
exercises.explanation: Before lunch the greeting is «Bom dia», and you can add the person's title: «Bom dia, senhor Costa!».
exercises.question: Como cumprimentas o teu vizinho às oito da manhã?

exercises.prompt: You did not catch the name of a stranger. Ask him to say it again.
exercises.explanation: To a stranger you use the formal «Pode repetir?»; «Podes repetir?» is the tu form.

exercises.prompt: You meet Dona Inês at five in the afternoon. Fill the three gaps.
exercises.explanation: «Tarde» is feminine, so «boa tarde»; Dona Inês gets the formal «Como está?»; and she is a woman, so she answers «obrigada».
exercises.template: — Boa ___, Dona Inês! Como ___? — Estou bem, ___.

exercises.prompt: Match each goodbye with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: The «até…» forms say when you meet again; «Adeus» is a final goodbye.

exercises.prompt: You are a man. Order a coffee politely and thank the waiter.
exercises.explanation: «Por favor» comes after the request, and a man thanks with «obrigado». In Lisbon a small espresso is «uma bica».

exercises.prompt: What does the word in bold mean?
exercises.explanation: «Adeus» is a goodbye for when you will not see the person soon; for later today say «Até logo».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong in this European Portuguese sentence.
exercises.explanation: European Portuguese uses «estar a + infinitivo»: «estou a falar ao telefone». The gerund «falando» is Brazilian.

exercises.prompt: Beatriz meets her new teacher for the first time. Put the dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: A polite first meeting goes: greeting, checking who the person is, «muito prazer», «como está?», then asking to come in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bom dia! Desculpe, é o professor Soares?

exercises.prompt: You are talking to a stranger who speaks too fast. Fill the three gaps.
exercises.explanation: «Não percebo» = I don't understand; with a stranger you keep the formal «Pode repetir?» and add «por favor».

exercises.prompt: You point at a zebra crossing and want to know the Portuguese word for it. Ask.
exercises.explanation: «Como se diz … em português?» is the fixed question for asking a word; «se diz» is impersonal, so the verb stays in the third person.
acceptedAnswers: Como é que se diz isto em português?

exercises.prompt: It is Friday evening at the office. Wish your colleague a good weekend and say you will see her on Monday.
exercises.explanation: «Fim» is masculine, so «bom fim de semana»; for the next meeting you use «até + day»: «até segunda».

exercises.prompt: Write your own goodbye.
exercises.explanation: On a Friday people really do say «Bom fim de semana!» plus «Até + day» for the next meeting.
exercises.question: Como te despedes dos colegas à sexta-feira?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Até segunda! Bom fim de semana!

exercises.prompt: A student is speaking to the school secretary. One word is wrong.
exercises.explanation: With «a senhora» everything stays formal: «Desculpe». «Desculpa» is the tu form, for friends.

exercises.prompt: Your friend Rita looks tired. Ask her how she is, using her name.
exercises.explanation: Rita is a friend, so you use the tu form: «Como estás, Rita?».
exercises.givenAnswer: Estou um pouco cansada, mas tudo bem.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the usual informal question.
exercises.explanation: The fixed informal question is «Tudo bem?», literally 'everything well?'.

exercises.prompt: It is 11 p.m. and you are leaving a friend's house. Say goodbye and tell her you will see her tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: After dark «boa noite» is also a goodbye, and «até amanhã» tells your friend when you meet again.
